sport: Jumping events (long jump, triple jump, high jump)
scope_notes: Covers the approach run, long jump penultimate step/take-off, long jump flight & landing, triple jump phases, high jump curved approach/take-off and bar clearance, plus general jump-landing mechanics for plyometric training. Pole vault is not covered.
source_gap_notes: Good research base (World Athletics biomechanics reports, Dapena's high jump work, Hay's triple jump review, Linthorne's take-off angle study). Coaching drill sources are thinner online; long jump flight styles and landing rely more on coaching consensus.

sources.name: World Athletics - Biomechanical Report, Men's Long Jump, 2017 IAAF World Championships London
sources.credibility: Official elite data: penultimate stride ~6% longer, final stride ~9% shorter; take-off contact ~0.12-0.13 s.

sources.name: Myers B - Improving the penultimate step in the jumping events (IAAF New Studies in Athletics 1989)
sources.credibility: University of Arizona head coach; take-off goals (<10% horizontal velocity loss, 15-25 deg take-off), penultimate mechanics and analysis by sound.

sources.name: Linthorne NP, Guzman MS, Bridgett LA - Optimum take-off angle in the long jump (J Sports Sci 2005)
sources.credibility: Athlete-specific optimum take-off angle ~23 deg (competition 19-25 deg) because speed drops at steeper angles.

sources.name: Dapena J - Mechanics of rotation in the Fosbury-flop (Med Sci Sports Exerc 1980)
sources.credibility: Most angular momentum for bar clearance is generated during take-off.

sources.name: Dapena J et al. - Why do high jumpers use a curved approach?
sources.credibility: Curve lets the jumper lean away from the bar (lowering the COM without deep knee flexion) and helps generate somersault rotation.

sources.name: Dapena J - The evolution of high jumping technique: biomechanical analysis (overview PDF)
sources.credibility: Overview of bar-clearance principles, run-up speed vs free-limb actions (double-arm, lead leg).

sources.name: Hay JG - The biomechanics of the triple jump: a review (J Sports Sci 1992)
sources.credibility: Phase-ratio framework (hop-, balanced-, jump-dominated) and determinants of distance.

sources.name: Optimisation of phase ratio in the triple jump using computer simulation (Human Movement Science 2016)
sources.credibility: Simulation: optimal phase ratio depends on the athlete's strength/velocity conversion; no universal ideal.

sources.name: Biomechanical Evaluation of the Phases of the Triple Jump Take-Off in a Top Female Athlete (J Hum Kinet, PMC)
sources.credibility: Case analysis of take-off kinematics across hop, step and jump.

sources.name: NSCA - Plyometric Implementation: Setup and Execution of Jump Landing Positions to Decrease Likelihood of Injuries
sources.credibility: National Strength and Conditioning Association education on landing positions.

sources.name: SimpliFaster - Building a Better Technical Model for the Long Jump

skills.name: Approach run (long/triple jump)
skills.recommended_camera: Side view panning or fixed at the last 6 strides; plus board-level camera.

checkpoints.description: Consistent, accelerating approach that reaches controllable near-maximal speed at the board, with posture rising to upright in the final strides.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: trunk near vertical in last 4-6 strides; step-length pattern consistent between trials (+/- ~5-10 cm at check marks)

checkpoints.description: Rhythm increases in the last two steps (quicker turnover).
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: last two contact-to-contact times shorter than preceding strides

faults.name: Inconsistent approach / stutter to hit the board
faults.video_signs: Visible stride adjustment (chopping or reaching) in the last strides.
faults.correction_cue: 'Run the same rhythm every time - trust the mark.'
faults.why_it_matters: Late adjustments cost speed and disrupt the penultimate step.

drills.name: Check-mark approach runs
drills.setup: Runway with a start mark and a coach check mark ~6 strides out.
steps: Run full approaches without jumping, running through the board.
Coach records where the take-off foot lands relative to the board and the check mark.
Adjust the start mark; repeat until consistent.
drills.why: Repeated run-throughs build a reproducible stride pattern so the athlete arrives at the board without adjustments.

skills.name: Long jump penultimate step and take-off
skills.recommended_camera: Side view at board level, perpendicular, 120-240 fps.

checkpoints.description: Penultimate stride slightly longer and the final stride shorter (elite: ~6% longer and ~9% shorter than prior strides); final steps 'pulled' under the body, not reached.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: penultimate step length > final step length by ~5-10%

checkpoints.description: Centre of mass lowered slightly on the penultimate step (flat, slightly heel-first contact), then rising through take-off.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: hip height dips a few cm on the penultimate contact, then rises at take-off

checkpoints.description: Take-off foot plants quickly and actively, nearly flat, with a brief contact (~0.12-0.13 s in elite men).
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: take-off contact frames x (1/fps) ~0.11-0.14 s for elite; shin slightly behind vertical at touchdown

checkpoints.description: Take-off angle well below 45 degrees - typically ~18-25 deg (athlete-specific optimum ~23 deg) - while losing less than ~10% horizontal velocity.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: angle of hip trajectory in the first frames after toe-off ~18-25 deg

checkpoints.description: At toe-off: take-off leg fully extended, free thigh driven up to ~horizontal, trunk upright, arms blocking.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: take-off knee ~170-180 deg; free thigh near horizontal; trunk within ~10 deg of vertical

faults.name: Reaching final step (braking take-off)
faults.video_signs: Long last stride with the foot planted far ahead; obvious braking and loss of speed.
faults.correction_cue: 'Shorten the last step - quick-quick off the board.'
faults.why_it_matters: A reaching take-off kills horizontal velocity, the main determinant of distance.

faults.name: No penultimate lowering (running off the board)
faults.video_signs: No change in rhythm or COM height; athlete runs through with a flat trajectory.
faults.correction_cue: 'Long-short rhythm: lower on the penultimate, up through the board.'
faults.why_it_matters: Without the penultimate preparation there is little vertical velocity.

faults.name: Jumping too steep
faults.video_signs: Athlete slows and 'pops' up at a high angle.
faults.correction_cue: 'Run off the board, not up into the sky.'
faults.why_it_matters: Steeper take-offs reduce take-off speed; the optimum is far below 45 deg.

drills.name: Short-approach (4-6 stride) take-off drill
drills.setup: Short approach into the pit; coach stands beside the board listening.
steps: Run 4-6 strides emphasizing a long-short rhythm on the last two steps.
Take off into a tall 'take-off position' and land in the pit.

Coach listens to the last two contacts: loud, blocking contacts = braking (over-long step); ordinary sprint sound = running through with no conversion; correct = a resonant penultimate contact followed by a quicker take-off step (a distinct speed-up of the rhythm).
drills.fixes: Reaching final step; no penultimate lowering; jumping too steep
drills.why: Short approaches allow many quality take-off repetitions; Myers shows coaches can detect correct penultimate mechanics by the sound/rhythm of the last two contacts.

pro_tips.tip: Coach the take-off by ear as well as by eye: correct penultimate mechanics produce a distinctive quick rhythm on the last two contacts.
The athlete-specific optimum take-off angle (~23 deg in experienced jumpers) is low because jumping steeper costs more take-off speed than it gains in height.

checkpoints.description: Heels extended forward at landing with hips brought forward/collapsed past the heels to avoid falling back.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: heels ahead of the hip at first sand contact; hips then move forward over the heels

faults.name: Sitting back on landing
faults.video_signs: Athlete falls back into the sand behind the heel marks.
faults.correction_cue: 'Feet out, then drive the hips forward through the knees.'
faults.why_it_matters: Measurement is from the closest mark - falling back loses distance.

skills.name: Triple jump (hop-step-jump)
skills.recommended_camera: Side view panning along the runway, 120+ fps.

checkpoints.description: Phase distribution is individual: elite jumpers commonly show roughly 35-37% hop, ~30% step, 33-36% jump; avoid an over-long hop that collapses the step.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: phase % = phase distance / total; flag if step < ~28% (collapsed step)

checkpoints.description: Flat, low hop take-off (lower angle than the long jump) to preserve horizontal speed.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: hop take-off trajectory angle lower than the athlete's long jump take-off angle

checkpoints.description: Active, 'pawing' landings under the body for each phase with an upright trunk.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: touchdown foot close to below hip; trunk within ~10-15 deg of vertical at each contact

faults.name: Over-big hop / collapsed step
faults.video_signs: Very high/long hop followed by a short step as the leg collapses on landing.
faults.correction_cue: 'Hop flat and fast - save something for the step.'
faults.why_it_matters: Excess hop height increases landing load and the step collapses.

faults.name: Leaning forward on landings
faults.video_signs: Trunk tips forward at hop/step landings.
faults.why_it_matters: Forward lean disrupts the next take-off.

drills.name: Rhythm bounding (hop-hop-step-step)
drills.setup: Runway or grass; cones at even spacing.
steps: Land actively under the hips with upright trunk; keep rhythm even.
drills.why: Even-rhythm bounding builds the elastic strength and landing posture needed for balanced phases.

pro_tips.tip: There is no universal optimal phase ratio; it depends on how efficiently the athlete converts horizontal to vertical velocity.

skills.name: High jump (Fosbury flop) curved approach and take-off
skills.recommended_camera: Rear/front view along the curve and side view at take-off, 120+ fps.

checkpoints.description: J-shaped approach: straight run then a curve of ~4-5 strides; on the curve the body leans away from the bar (inward lean).
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: whole-body lean toward curve centre ~ visible (e.g., > ~10 deg from vertical in front view) on curve strides

checkpoints.description: Curve allows a low COM without deep knee bend; the jumper moves from inward lean to vertical at take-off.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: take-off knee flexion moderate (not deep squat); body near vertical at toe-off

checkpoints.description: Quick, flat, pulling penultimate step with deeper knee flexion than in the long jump, and an EARLY take-off plant (take-off leg used like a vault pole); take-off angle much steeper (~45-55 deg) than the horizontal jumps.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: take-off foot ahead of the hip at touchdown; take-off trajectory ~45-55 deg

checkpoints.description: Double-arm action: during the penultimate step both arms pull back to about hip level, then drive up through take-off.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: both wrists behind the hip line on the penultimate contact; above shoulder height at toe-off

checkpoints.description: Drive the free knee and arms upward forcefully at take-off.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: free thigh near horizontal and arms above shoulder height at toe-off

faults.name: Running straight at the bar / drifting
faults.video_signs: Approach flattens; jumper turns into the bar at take-off and drifts along it.
faults.correction_cue: 'Run the curve - lean away from the bar.'
faults.why_it_matters: Without the curve the athlete must squat to lower the COM and cannot rotate efficiently.

faults.name: Over-long take-off step
faults.video_signs: Final step reaches far ahead; loud blocking contact; jumper drives into the bar rather than up.
faults.correction_cue: 'Quick last two - plant early, not far.'
faults.why_it_matters: Myers notes this is where many young high jumpers go wrong: it hinders converting horizontal to vertical velocity and blunts the stretch reflex.

faults.name: Leaning into the bar at take-off
faults.video_signs: Shoulders lean toward the bar during take-off.
faults.correction_cue: 'Stay tall - go up, let the rotation come.'
faults.why_it_matters: Most rotation is generated during take-off; leaning in disrupts it and brings the body down onto the bar.

drills.name: Circle runs with pop-ups
drills.setup: Mark a circle or J-curve (~5 strides) on the track/apron.
steps: Run the circle leaning inward from the ankles.
Every few strides, perform a pop-up take-off driving the free knee and arms.
Progress to curve approach + scissor jump, then full flop at low height.
drills.fixes: Running straight; leaning into the bar
drills.why: Circle running builds the inward lean the curve is supposed to create, and pop-ups rehearse transitioning to vertical at take-off.

pro_tips.tip: High jump style trade-off: some jumpers rely on a faster run-up, others on stronger double-arm or lead-leg actions to increase take-off force.

skills.name: High jump bar clearance
skills.recommended_camera: Side view perpendicular to the bar.

checkpoints.description: Arch over the bar so body parts are lowered around the bar while the centre of mass peaks; then lift the legs as the hips pass.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: hip highest point with head and knees lower (arch) as hips cross the bar

faults.name: Early leg lift / sitting
faults.video_signs: Hips drop onto the bar because legs lift too early.
faults.correction_cue: 'Hips up - wait, then kick the legs.'
faults.why_it_matters: Mistimed segment movements lower the hips relative to the bar.

pro_tips.tip: Dapena: more effective bar clearance means lowering some body parts so the bar can be higher for a given centre-of-mass peak.

skills.name: Jump landing mechanics (plyometric / training)
skills.recommended_camera: Front view for knee alignment and side view for flexion.

checkpoints.description: Quiet, soft landings with hips back and knees tracking over the midfoot/second toe; no inward knee collapse.
checkpoints.measurable_angle_or_rule: knee valgus angle < ~10-15 deg in front view; knee flexion > ~60 deg during absorption

faults.name: Knee valgus / stiff landing
faults.video_signs: Knees cave inward; loud heel slaps; locked knees.
faults.why_it_matters: These are the cues NSCA uses to stop a plyometric set.

drills.name: Low drop-landing 'stick' progression
steps: Step off and land on both feet, holding the landing 2 s.
Check knees over toes, hips back, quiet landing.
Progress to jumps, then single-leg, and only later to reactive drop jumps.
drills.why: Mastering landing positions at low heights before reactive jumps reduces injury risk.
